transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because there’s been… some trouble with a work contract. Environmental modeling.

I’m pretty sure people on it have been tracking my revisions and putting errors into the datasets, so it looks like I can’t lead the work. My wife and some of the junior analysts keep saying it’s just version-control problems, but… I don’t think that’s all it is.
Do you think someone is intentionally trying to harm your reputation at work?

Yes. I mean… I can’t prove every piece of it, but it looks intentional to me. The revisions I make get tracked, and then errors show up in the datasets in ways that make me look like I don’t know what I’m doing. Others say it’s just version-control mistakes, but I don’t buy that.
How long have you been thinking that someone is intentionally trying to harm your reputation at work?
For about… two months, I’d say. That’s when I started feeling pretty sure they were tracking my revisions and putting those errors in.
Have you felt like anyone else is out to get you, outside of work?
Not really outside of that contract, no. It’s mostly the people tied to the environmental modeling work… the revisions, the datasets. That’s where it’s happening.
Have your thoughts about people intentionally harming your reputation at work changed at all over the past two months?

They’ve gotten stronger, I guess. At first I wondered if it was just sloppy file handling, but now… I’m pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract are tracking my revisions and planting errors so it looks like I can’t lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts say it’s version-control stuff, but I don’t really believe that.
Can you think of any situation where you might be wrong about people intentionally putting errors in your datasets?

I mean… I suppose it’s possible. My wife says it’s just version-control mistakes, and the junior analysts say the same kind of thing. But it doesn’t feel that way to me. It feels like they’re tracking my revisions and putting errors in so I look like I can’t lead it.
Do you think the people who are supposedly sabotaging your work are doing it for a reason that doesn't make sense to other people?

I don’t know if it doesn’t make sense. To me it makes sense… they don’t want me leading that contract, so they track my revisions and slip errors into the datasets. Other people say it’s just version-control mistakes, but I don’t buy that.
Have you ever considered that you might be overestimating the intentions of your coworkers?

I’ve considered it because people keep saying that. My wife, the junior analysts… they say it’s version-control mistakes. But I don’t know. It still seems like they’re tracking my revisions and putting errors in on purpose so I look bad leading the work.
Have you ever had a time, even for a short period, where you didn't think people were intentionally sabotaging your work?

Maybe for a minute here and there, when someone explains it as version-control stuff. But it doesn’t really last. I keep coming back to the same thing — that they’re tracking my revisions and putting errors in so I look like I can’t lead the contract.
Do you think the belief that people are sabotaging your work is something that most people would understand and agree with, or is it something that might seem strange to others?

Most people probably think it sounds strange. My wife does, and the junior analysts keep saying it’s just version-control mistakes. But to me it still looks like they’re tracking my revisions and putting errors in the datasets so I can’t lead the work.
How much time would you say you spend thinking about the people sabotaging your work each day?

A lot of the day, honestly. I don’t sit there timing it, but it keeps coming back whenever I think about the contract or the datasets. Maybe... several hours altogether. It’s hard not to notice when I’m pretty sure they’re tracking my revisions.
Has there ever been a time when you completely stopped believing that people were sabotaging your work?

No... not completely. I might doubt it for a little while if someone says it’s just version-control mistakes, but I don’t really stop believing it. It keeps coming back that they’re tracking my revisions and putting errors in the datasets.
Has your belief that people are sabotaging your work at the environmental modeling contract ever completely gone away, even if only for a short time?

No. Maybe I’ve questioned it for a bit when people tell me it’s just version-control stuff, but it doesn’t really go away. It still seems like they’re tracking my revisions and putting mistakes in the datasets.
Has your belief that people are sabotaging your work changed in intensity over the past two months?

It’s... maybe gotten stronger, I guess. Not all at once, but over these weeks I’ve been noticing the revisions and the dataset errors more. When my wife or the junior analysts say it’s just version-control mistakes, I can hear that, but it doesn’t really settle it for me.
Has there ever been a day in the past two months where you didn't think about people sabotaging your work at all?
No... I don’t think so. Maybe it wasn’t in my head every minute, but pretty much every day something with the revisions or the datasets would make me think they were doing it.
Has your belief that people are sabotaging your work ever been completely absent from your mind for more than a day?
No... not more than a day. It’s there, maybe quieter sometimes, but I still think they’re tracking my revisions or putting errors in the datasets.
Has your belief that people are sabotaging your work ever completely disappeared, even if just for a little while?
No... I wouldn’t say it completely disappeared. Sometimes I can push it aside for a bit, but then something with the revisions or the datasets comes up, and it’s right back there.
Do you think your belief that people are sabotaging your work could be considered irrational by others?

I suppose they might say that. My wife does sometimes, and the junior analysts say it’s just version-control mistakes. But… from where I’m sitting, it looks like they’re tracking my revisions and putting errors in the datasets.
Do you think there's any chance at all that you're mistaken about people sabotaging your work?

Maybe a small chance, I guess… if everyone else is right about the version-control mistakes. But I don’t really believe that. It looks too much like they’re tracking my revisions and planting errors in the datasets.
